speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Can you describe the specific appearance of the skin lesions, and have you noticed any similar lesions on your other joints or skin? Also, did you recall seeing a "bull's-eye" rash or any tick bites during your camping trip in Minnesota?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The violaceous vesiculopustular lesions are a very specific finding. Have you noticed any lesions on your palms, soles, or mucous membranes, and have you had any recent exposure to water like swimming in lakes or rivers?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of recent camping in Minnesota, migratory joint pain, and violaceous vesiculopustular lesions strongly suggests Spotted Fever Group Rickettsiosis, likely Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever. I need to confirm systemic involvement and check for characteristic signs before finalizing. Have you experienced a headache or nausea, and can you tell me if the rash has spread to your wrists and ankles or started on your extremities?
